title: Bill Borden and recording Bix's piano pieces
summary: Bill Borden asked at the Hot Platter Club for something to record, leading him to work out Bix's piano pieces for a 1974 album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How did that come about? Who sought you out.
George Wein had called up one time --
This was before the Wein thing, wasn't it. This Beiderbecke thing.
Oh, Bill Borden -- oh, you mean this. Oh, yeah, well, that's only about two or three years ago.
But I think it was before the Wein and Goldkette thing.
Yes, I guess it was. Yeah, that's right.
This was recorded in '74. So that's five years ago.
That's right. Well, see, I went over to -- I was going over to Jersey and this Platter Club over
Kind of an offshoot of the New Jersey Jazz Society.

Right. They asked me -- oh, Bill Borden is a member of it, and they mentioned in New Jersey Jazz who their guests are and I went over there with my brother and Bill saw us and so he came up and he says, "I just come up to see you. I wondered what happened to you." Well, nothing much. He said, "You got anything around that you would like to record?" and I guess he thought I was a real hot jazz man.
"Anything of Beiderbecke's?" Well, I said, "I have the piano pieces," but that's recorded in 1904, that took me a little while to do --

1974, I'd say at least 1973 that was working, because I'm not had another guitar player, and had to work that out, and I couldn't get in touch with -- I couldn't (Bucky Pizzarelli -- ed.) get Bucky because he's busy so I had to piece a couple of things here, piece a couple of things here and work on it, gradually, over and over and over and I finally got the things together, and let's see, the Wein thing came up about that time, I think.
